finance__procurement___index.md:233:- The first page of the Zip request includes anticorruption gating question (e.g., will the vendor interact with government agencies on our behalf, was this vendor recommended by a government official, etc.). If the answer to any of these questions is “yes,” the Ethics & Compliance team must consider whether the vendor presents unacceptably high compliance risk.
finance__procurement___index.md:365:1. After all executive approvals are received, the Zip request(s) should be created to document official approvals, obtain signatures on contracts, and release PO(s).
communication___index.md:164:[Omitted long matching line]
communication___index.md:256:[Informal communication](/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/informal-communication/) is made up of interactions between co-workers that are unofficial in nature and focus on building social relationships outside of the normal hierarchy of a typical business structure.
communication___index.md:1045:- Storing official company records or documents
finance__expenses.md:33:- Managers are expected to review their team's expenses in their entirety every month, and must flag any concerns immediately to the Accounts Payable team. Potential violations of GitLab's [Gifts & Entertainment Policy](/handbook/legal/policies/gifts-contributions/#gifts-and-entertainment-policy) should also be flagged to the Legal department, as necessary.  
finance__expenses.md:42:- Provide clear and timely feedback to Team Members and managers regarding missing information, general questions, or "out of policy" issues, and escalate potential violations of the gifts and entertainment expense rules to the Legal department in a manner consistent with GitLab's [Whistleblower Policy](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1kB3k5FRnR3OUBP0Eyo3SxxyPKeiRFfUk).
finance__expenses.md:54:- Expenses for gifts and entertainment must be incurred and reimbursed in accordance with GitLab's [Gifts & Entertainment Policy](/handbook/legal/policies/gifts-contributions/#gifts-and-entertainment-policy) and [Antibribery Policy](/handbook/legal/anti-corruption-policy/).
finance__expenses.md:63:- Personal credits and gift cards: GitLab will reimburse only the actual out-of-pocket amount paid by the employee. If personal credits, gift cards, rewards points, or other discounts are applied to a business purchase, reimbursement will be limited to the net amount charged to the employee's personal payment method.
finance__expenses.md:64:Example: An employee purchases a $100 monitor and applies a $50 gift card. GitLab will reimburse $50 (the amount actually paid), not the pre-discount price of $100.
finance__expenses.md:222:- If you decide to stay with friends or family instead of a hotel / Airbnb for a business trip, you may expense up to a $50 appropriate host/hostess gift.
finance__expenses.md:481:### Team Member Significant Life Events and Team Member Gifts
finance__expenses.md:483:- Cash or cash equivalents, such as gift cards, are not allowed; Qualified gifts are capped at $125 per transaction.
finance__expenses.md:484:- Managers are able to send Gifts and Flowers on behalf of their team members in acknowledgment of significant life events such as well wishes ahead of surgery, or the loss of a loved one. Baby gifts are not reimbursable as GitLab already sends them a [gift](/handbook/people-group/celebrations/#new-parent-swag).
finance__expenses.md:485:- Any People Manager can send a gift or flowers to any Team Member at GitLab to let them know they are thinking about them. Examples include:
finance__expenses.md:486:  - A new Team Member recently purchased a new home and shared their news with others. A People Manager sends a "Home Sweet Home" doormat as a congratulatory gift.
finance__expenses.md:489:- The cost of the gifts and flowers provided to GitLab Team Members will be allocated to the senders departmental budget. The allowable cost for gifts is up to $125 USD (including shipping) per gift.
finance__expenses.md:490:- If you would like to buy holiday gifts for your team, these need to be done personally and should not be expensed.
finance__expenses.md:491:- People Managers are to use their own personal card for expense reimbursement. People Managers will need to be sure to use Team `EmployeeGiftsFlowers` and the account 6028 in Navan Expense for the expense.
finance__expenses.md:492:- For further questions regarding expensing of gifts and flowers, please reach out to the AP team by submitting a request under the `Expenses -> General Expenses` page of [Compass](/handbook/eta/corporate-it/compass/compass-guide/).
finance__expenses.md:496:- **Expense Type / Navan Policy Category:** Gifts - internal
finance__expenses.md:497:- **Classification:** EmployeeGiftsFlowers
finance__expenses.md:554:- Team Members are prohibited from providing anything of value, including meals, to any government official, government Team Member, or government representative (including any government prospects and government customers).
finance__expenses.md:631:- For conferences, any gifts or swag related items to be given out are not to be expensed.
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:12:GitLab and Team Members and Partners are prohibited from authorizing, making, offering, promising, requesting, receiving or accepting bribes or accepting kickbacks in any form.  This prohibition applies to all forms of bribery, including commercial bribery as well as bribery of government employees or officials.
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:14:[Omitted long matching line]
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:18:1. payments made directly to a government employee or official for an improper purpose;
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:19:1. payments or gifts to third parties where Team Members and Partners know or have reason to know that at least a portion of the payments or gifts is likely to be offered by the third party to a government employee or official for an improper purpose;
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:21:1. payments to retain assets, such as an "under the table" payment to a tax official to settle a tax claim.
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:27:**Who is a "government official"?**
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:28:"Government official" includes:
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:30:1. any official or employee of a government, including any political party, administrative agency, or government-owned business;
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:31:1. any person acting in an official capacity on behalf of a government entity;
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:32:1. employees or agents of a business which is owned or controlled by a government;
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:33:1. any person or firm employed by or acting for or on behalf of any government;
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:34:1. any political party official, employee or agent of a political party, or candidate for political office (or political party position); and
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:37:Any doubts about whether a particular person is a government official should be resolved by assuming that the individual involved is a government official for purposes of the FCPA or the Anti-Corruption Laws.
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:40:"Anything of value" includes money and monetary equivalents (such as gambling chips and gift cards), entertainment, accommodations, and any other benefit.  There is no "minimum" required under the FCPA – any amount can be sufficient to trigger a violation.
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:45:1. influence a decision by a government official, including a failure to perform their official functions;
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:46:1. induce a government official to use their influence to affect a decision by someone else in their government; and
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:47:1. induce a government official to use their influence to affect or influence any act or decision.
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:51:### GIFTS, ENTERTAINMENT, TRAVEL & PROMOTIONAL EXPENDITURES
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:53:Gifts in the business context can be an appropriate way for businesspeople to display respect for each other.  GitLab expects the use of good judgment and moderation when giving or receiving entertainment or gifts.  No gift or entertainment should ever be offered, given, provided or accepted by Team Members and Partners unless it:
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:63:[Omitted long matching line]
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:65:1. Significant legal restrictions apply with regard to providing gifts, entertainment, travel and promotional expenditures related to government officials.  Team Members and Partners must make sure they fully understand all such restrictions and associated policies and procedures.  In each instance:
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:66:    1. all gifts, entertainment, or promotional expenses which are intended to induce a government employee or official to misuse their position or to obtain an improper advantage are prohibited, regardless of their value;
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:68:    1. gifts must be of token value (such as shirts or tote bags that reflect Company's business name and/or logo), legal and customary, and openly given; and
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:69:    1. expenses and gifts must be fully and accurately reflected in the Company's books and records and backed by receipts.
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:71:Team Members and Partners should avoid even the appearance of impropriety.  Any gift or expense that is lavish or might otherwise prove embarrassing for the Company is prohibited.  If Team Members and Partners have any question regarding the appropriateness of any gift or expense, they should consult GitLab's Chief Legal Officer prior to giving the gift or incurring the expense.
legal__anti-corruption-policy.md:82:- whether the third party has personal or professional ties to the government or any government official;

content.text: The documents conflict. The anti-corruption policy allows gifts to government officials only if they are of token value (for example, a shirt or tote bag with the company logo), legal and customary, openly given, and recorded with receipts. Gifts meant to gain an improper advantage are banned at any value. The expenses page, though, says team members may not give anything of value, including meals, to government officials or employees. Check with the Chief Legal Officer before giving anything.

result: The documents conflict. The anti-corruption policy allows gifts to government officials only if they are of token value (for example, a shirt or tote bag with the company logo), legal and customary, openly given, and recorded with receipts. Gifts meant to gain an improper advantage are banned at any value. The expenses page, though, says team members may not give anything of value, including meals, to government officials or employees. Check with the Chief Legal Officer before giving anything.
